chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'When should a man shorten [his prayer] when he intends to travel?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'When he loses sight of the houses.' I said, 'The man intends to travel, so he goes out when the sun declines.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'When you go out, pray two rak'at.' And al-Husayn ibn Sa'id reported from Safwan and Fadalah, from al-Ala', similar to it.

key_terms.تَوَارَى مِنَ الْبُيُوت: Losing sight of the houses (city limits)

ai.seo_question: When does the ruling of shortening prayer begin for a traveler according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the precise moment the state of travel (safar) commences for the purpose of shortening prayers, defining it as the point when the traveler exits the city limits and loses sight of its dwellings. The instruction to pray two rak'at upon exiting highlights the immediate applicability of the travel ruling, reflecting the Shia juristic consensus on the physical boundary of the city as the threshold for legal change. This narration underscores the practical ease Islam affords travelers, linking the physical act of departure directly to the modification of worship obligations.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahy, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘A man intends the journey, when should he shorten (the Salāt)?’ Heasws said, ‘When he loses sight of the houses’. I said, ‘The man intends the journey, so he goes out when the sun (starts to) decline’. Heasws said: ‘When he goes out, so he prays two Rak’at of Salāt’. And Al-Husayn Bin Saeed reported from Safwan and Fazalat, from Al-A’ala – similar to it.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who wants to travel. Where is he required to apply the rules about journey? He (the Imam) said, ‘He must apply them where houses become invisible to him? I then asked, ‘A man begins his journey on Zawal (declining of the sun toward the west at noontime). What is he required to do? 5 He (the Imam) said, ‘When you come out perform two Rak‘at Salah prayers).’ Also al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id has narrated from, Safwan and Fadalah from al-‘Ala’ a similar Hadith.”
